src/mailer/mailer.service.ts: `sendMail({ templatePath, context, ...mailOptions })` reads the template with `fs.readFile` and renders it with `Handlebars.compile(template, { strict: true })(context)`. The rendering only serves to build the outgoing email.

src/mailer/mailer.service.ts: the default `from` value is built once from mail.defaultName and mail.defaultEmail, and `html: mailOptions.html ? mailOptions.html : html` is the only HTML fallback rule.
src/mailer/mailer.service.ts: the only sending path is `this.transporter.sendMail(...)`, so the class always uses its own transporter.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is a single file, src/mailer/mailer.service.ts, and it handles one concern: sending email. It sets up a nodemailer transporter from the mail.* config keys, optionally turns a Handlebars template into HTML, and fills in a default sender. Template rendering and the default sender are both part of preparing an outgoing message, so the file does not split into unrelated concerns. Each rule lives in one place: the transport settings are read once in the constructor, and the default sender and HTML fallback are each decided once in sendMail. The service always sends through its own transporter field and never works around it. Because the unit has only one file, there is no second file where a rule could be duplicated.
